scope: Authored v4 interfaces, documentation and examples. Product migration is outside this foundation.
verificationNote: Each rule's detect field names who catches a break. lint rules are enforced by npm run ui:lint, which only lets its baseline shrink. test rules name the test that exercises them. review rules depend on a person or agent reading the change.
protectedContent: Preserve code, commands, identifiers, protocol payloads, legal and license text, quoted material and user-entered values exactly. Prose rules do not rewrite their contents. Scope an exception to the exact element or data field; do not exempt its ordinary UI siblings. Never put real secrets in examples, diagnostics or captures.

rules.title: Preserve the Infisical identity
rules.instruction: Use warm neutral surfaces, Archivo, Geist Mono and square corners everywhere (there is no radius scale and no corner mode). Primary (and default) Buttons are the ink fill for the one main action; accent Buttons use the shared accent finish for a page's one primary create action (rule/accent-create) and for approval and grant moments. Keep selection neutral. Pair brand lime fills with on-accent ink, not light-theme lime text.
rules.good: One ink primary Button for the task's main action, an accent Button only for the page's create action or an approval, and neutral alternatives and selection.
rules.avoid: A locally painted gradient, third font or pill-shaped control introduced by an example.

rules.title: Paint with color tokens
rules.instruction: Take every color from a v4 token: the --v4-* custom properties or the Tailwind roles mapped onto them. A literal hex, rgb or hsl value, or a Tailwind palette class, bypasses both themes and the contrast pairs.
rules.good: bg-background text-muted-foreground, or var(--v4-scrim) for an overlay.
rules.avoid: bg-black/10 on a dialog overlay, or color: #fbfbf9 in a component stylesheet.

rules.title: Give every border a line color
rules.instruction: A border width utility (border, border-t, border-x and the rest) names its color in the same class string, usually line-soft: border-[color:var(--v4-line-soft)] for an edge or a divider that meets one, and var(--v4-line) only for a standalone rule (rule/line-roles). A bare border falls back to the global gray, which reads as a bright stripe in dark mode.
rules.good: border-t border-[color:var(--v4-line-soft)] on a dialog footer.
rules.avoid: border-t alone on a footer, or border on a menu with no color.

rules.title: Frame tables and lists; keep standalone cards plain
rules.instruction: Tables are framed: a standalone DataTable sits in the tint frame, and a DataTable inside a framed Card, List or other frame drops its frame and embeds on the card's inset surface. The frameless native Table is for the secrets overview matrix and for a table inside a Dialog, Sheet or Popover; a table inside a Card is an embedded DataTable (rule/detail-card-data-table). Lists default to framed and change case by case. A standalone Card is plain, the default, or no card at all; set variant="framed" only for emphasis, such as the org overview product cards, or for a section card that heads part of a page, such as a detail sidecar or a settings section. A plain Card pads raw children by the same inset as a framed Card body.
rules.good: A DataTable in its frame on a list page, a plain Card for a standalone summary, and <Card variant="framed" title="Details"> in a DetailLayout sidecar.
rules.avoid: A framed Card wrapped around every block on a page, or a standalone Card set to variant framed with no emphasis or section role.

detect.how: Check each Card that sets variant framed is emphasis or a section card.

rules.title: Never nest one frame in another
rules.instruction: A framed container never renders inside another framed container. Card, DataTable, List, ApprovalQueue and CodeBlock read the frame context: inside a framed Card, a framed List, a DataTable or a CodeBlock, a framed Card drops to plain, a DataTable and a framed List or ApprovalQueue embed frameless on the parent's inset surface, and a CodeBlock drops its tint frame. Overlays (Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Popover, HoverCard) start a fresh surface, so a frame inside one draws normally. Never write variant="framed" on a container inside a framed parent to force a second frame back on.
rules.good: A DataTable inside <Card variant="framed" title="Recently deleted" flush>, which renders as an embedded table on the card's inset with its header row on that surface.
rules.avoid: A List with variant="framed" inside a framed Card, or a tinted table frame sitting directly on a framed card's tint band so its header merges into the band.
rules.exceptions: The check reads containers written directly inside a framed parent in the same file. A framed child rendered from another component drops its frame at runtime and logs a development warning when it was asked for variant framed. Bordered boxes drawn by page stylesheets are caught by page-css-frame (rule/page-boxes-from-primitives).

rules.title: Draw bordered boxes with primitives, not page stylesheets
rules.instruction: A page stylesheet under pages/v4 never draws a four-sided border, or an outline outside a focus state, around a box. A page CSS module cannot see the frame it lands in, so a bordered pane or value box rendered inside a framed Card, List or DataTable from another file nests a frame in a frame (rule/no-nested-frames). Use a primitive that reads the frame context (Card, Tile, List, CodeBlock), the frame's own head, section or inset, or the tint shade. One-sided dividers stay fine.
rules.good: A previous and next diff pane on its bad or ok wash with no border of its own inside a bordered change card, or an icon tile on the tint shade in a card header.
rules.avoid: A .pane with a four-sided status border holding a .box with its own border, inside a card that already draws one.
rules.exceptions: A box that stays bordered wherever it renders, such as a dashed dropzone, a color swatch or a standalone tile in a sheet, marks its rule with v4-check-ignore page-css-frame and the reason in a comment before the rule. Findings that predate the check sit in scripts/check-v4-baseline.json.

rules.title: Branch on the scheme, not the theme name
rules.instruction: Themes are named palettes (peach, pale, dark) declared in tokens.json themes.list, each with a light or dark scheme. Anything that differs between light and dark, such as an on-light logo, a chart cursor, a toast theme or an opacity swap, reads the scheme: [data-scheme="dark"] in CSS and useV4Scheme() in code. A new theme lists only the tokens it overrides and inherits the rest.
rules.good: :global(.v4[data-scheme="dark"]) .segment, or useV4Scheme() === "light" ? onLight : image.
rules.avoid: .v4[data-theme="dark"] in a stylesheet, which misses any later dark theme, or a theme name compared against light.

rules.title: Use line-soft for edges and line for standalone rules
rules.instruction: line-soft is the default border: the outward edge of every inset surface, card, plain list, table, popover, dialog and bordered tile or badge, the app shell chrome (the AppInset island, the band rule, the sidebar edge and separators) and every divider that touches one of those edges, such as row hairlines, cell dividers and dialog head and footer rules. Reserve line for a standalone rule that touches no other border: a section rule, the band's divider marks, a lone hr, a tree guide, the tab track, chart axes and grid lines.
rules.good: border: var(--v4-size-control-border) solid var(--v4-line-soft) on a card, and a line rule under a section heading that ends in open space.
rules.avoid: A four-sided line border on a card, panel or tile, or a line-soft section rule floating on the page.
rules.exceptions: Control borders (inputs, outline buttons, selects) keep their own control tokens; only a control that points at line moves to line-soft.

rules.title: Use the shared Button material
rules.instruction: For accent Buttons, use the shared light accent face (Infisical yellow, #e3f047) and its owned colored inset illumination in both themes. Keep the entire face light, all glow inside the control, paint below the label, the control stationary and keyboard focus separate. Do not add dark upper shading, narrow hard light rims, noise, patterns, outside or drop shadows, lift, scale or whole-button filters. Primary and default Buttons are the flat ink fill; other component fills and neutral selection retain their own roles.
rules.good: A shared lime Grant for 1 hour Button beside an ink primary and outline and ghost alternatives, with the same label while saving.
rules.avoid: A dark upper Button face, hard edge-light band, glow outside the control, local material replicas or lime paint on every selected row.
rules.exceptions: The canonical accent Button material owns its colored inset glow. This exception does not authorize shadows on other primitives or caller-created material.

rules.title: Give a page's create action the accent
rules.instruction: A page's primary create action uses the accent Button variant: the one action that adds a new item to what the page lists, such as Add new, Create key, Add rule, Invite members or New connection. Use at most one per page, in the page header or in the toolbar above the list it fills; tab panels under that header share it. Every other primary stays the ink primary Button: Save, Confirm, Submit, Download, Done, and the submit button of a sheet or dialog, including the Create at the foot of a create form. Empty-state actions and buttons inside sheets and dialogs stay ink, because the page header or toolbar already carries the accent. Destructive actions stay destructive, and approval and grant moments keep the accent.
rules.good: An accent Add new in the Secrets toolbar beside outline filter and download buttons, with the Create button inside its sheet in ink.
rules.avoid: Two accent Buttons on one page, an accent Save changes or Download, or an accent submit at the foot of a create sheet.

rules.title: Choose the role and its foreground
rules.instruction: Use semantic color pairs in both themes. Brand --v4-accent is distinct from the neutral shadcn bg-accent role.
rules.good: bg-primary with text-primary-foreground.
rules.avoid: A white label chosen by eye or a border token borrowed for body text.

rules.title: Make the main action clear
rules.instruction: Give one action the strongest emphasis within an active task region. A dialog can have its own primary action. Use lower emphasis for alternatives and destructive treatment for a destructive consequence.
rules.good: Save with an outlined Cancel in the same form footer.
rules.avoid: Create, import, cancel and delete all competing at the strongest emphasis.

rules.title: Use descriptions strategically
rules.instruction: Descriptions are optional, and a good one carries information the title cannot. Use them where they help: a one-sentence page lede, optionally ending in a Docs link; a one-line dialog or sheet subtitle that scopes its content; short lines that tell the cards in a set apart; and secondary row lines that carry a state or a value. Keep flavor that orients people. Do not write text that restates the title, a lede longer than one sentence, or a marketing tagline, and trim existing copy, including copy ported from main, to that standard rather than deleting it wholesale.
rules.good: Billing with Manage your plan, payment method and invoices. as its one-line subtitle; plan cards whose short lines say who each plan is for; a row reading Visa ending in 6008.
rules.avoid: Group details under a Details title, a three-sentence page intro, or a tagline such as Your team's complete security toolkit.

detect.how: Read each description: keep it if it scopes, distinguishes, states a value or orients in one sentence; cut it if it restates the title or sells.

rules.title: Name the action and consequence
rules.instruction: In authored labels and operational feedback, name the action, object and result in sentence case with straight quotes, so people can predict the change. Keep the operation's name through the action, its confirmation and its result. Cut em dashes, promotional adjectives, three-beat slogans, setup-then-correct phrasing, decorative emoji and celebratory filler because they replace task information.
rules.good: Revoke token, then Token revoked. Clients using it can no longer authenticate.
rules.avoid: Submit or Get started, a Remove token action that reports Credential disconnected, or a celebration that only repeats the heading.
rules.exceptions: Preserve exact code, commands, identifiers, legal text, quotations, user-entered values and platform-owned terminology. The exception applies to those contents, not surrounding authored prose. Continue and Next may name step navigation.

rules.title: Distinguish empty, filtered and failed
rules.instruction: Distinguish first use, no matches, missing permission and request failure. Name the actual condition and offer its applicable recovery. A request failure must not become an empty collection.
rules.good: No secrets match these filters, with Clear filters.
rules.avoid: Create your first secret after a filtered request failed or a search returned no matches.
rules.exceptions: A purely decorative example explicitly labeled as such.

rules.title: Keep the label visible
rules.instruction: Name each field with a short, persistent label in sentence case. Use the placeholder only for an example value, never as the label or as hidden instructions. Put instructions and constraints in associated helper text, put the correction beside the invalid field and pair invalid styling with that readable explanation.
rules.good: Project name above the input, with payments-api as the placeholder and helper text below.
rules.avoid: A placeholder as the only label, an uppercase PLEASE ENTER YOUR TOKEN NAME:, or a red border as the only error message.
rules.exceptions: Proper nouns, abbreviations and exact identifiers such as JWT or CLIENT_ID.

rules.title: Keep the theme across portals
rules.instruction: Wrap the workbench in V4Scope. Let its portal container carry fonts and colors outside the scroller.
rules.good: A dialog rendered through V4Scope's portal container keeps the workbench fonts and colors.
rules.avoid: Adding v4 theme classes to document.body.

rules.title: Prove the API and installation contract
rules.instruction: Read actual exports before copying an example. Report a missing capability instead of inventing a prop or duplicating a component. An installed primitive, a documented preview and a verified registry install are different claims.
rules.good: A real import, supported props, named limitations and a clean-consumer build.
rules.avoid: A ready badge inferred from a generated JSON file or a working-looking import for an unavailable component.

rules.title: Do not turn every section into a card
rules.instruction: Group a distinct task or resource when a container helps people identify it. Let headings, alignment and spacing separate ordinary subsections. Repeated identical boxes and nested cards around unrelated content hide which information belongs together.
rules.good: One settings group containing related fields, or aligned rows for comparable resources.
rules.avoid: A bordered box around every label/help pair or identical card layouts for unrelated tasks.
rules.exceptions: Repeated cards that represent actual distinct resources.

rules.title: Decoration must carry information
rules.instruction: Use numbering for a real sequence and icons for recognizable meaning. Remove section markers, icons and arrows that do not identify content or an available action. The same visual device on unrelated sections makes differences harder to see.
rules.good: Numbered steps in a setup wizard.
rules.avoid: 01, 02, 03 on unrelated settings groups.
rules.exceptions: Explicit teaching diagrams and ordered procedures. Functional pagination, breadcrumb, hierarchy, disclosure and external-link arrows stay.

rules.title: Use the declared type roles
rules.instruction: For component chrome and app examples, use Archivo and Geist Mono according to the declared type roles. Use mono for literal machine text or an owned metadata role; whole explanatory paragraphs in mono flatten the reading hierarchy. Distinguish headings with the supported scale rather than arbitrary sizes, weight patches, gradient text or italic accent words.
rules.good: Archivo prose with a Geist Mono key, or the supported Meta mono role.
rules.avoid: A mono help paragraph, gradient-filled heading or uppercase micro-label added to manufacture hierarchy.
rules.exceptions: Preserve exact identifiers, source code, supported metadata roles and typography specimens demonstrating a token.

rules.title: Align what the eye sees
rules.instruction: Compare adjacent control boxes, text baselines and icon-to-label spacing in the actual rendered cluster. Equal CSS heights are the starting measurement, not proof of equal visual weight. Fix the owned recipe when peer controls drift; do not compensate with caller padding or transforms.
rules.good: One centrally owned icon alignment correction.
rules.avoid: A caller adding a different top: 1px patch on each screen.
rules.exceptions: Approved asymmetric artwork, not ordinary action icons.

rules.title: Motion must have a named purpose
rules.instruction: When pointer hover identifies a row or card, keep its target stationary. Animate explicit properties only to show a named state change or origin. Moving targets impede pointer use; avoid hover lift, scale, added shadows, transition: all and delayed row entrances in a dense workbench.
rules.good: A stable row hover fill or the existing overlay transition tied to opening.
rules.avoid: A card lifting under the pointer or every table row sliding in on refresh.
rules.exceptions: Preserve canonical control states, reduced-motion-aware loaders and purposeful motion or data-visualization specimens. Document the local purpose.

rules.title: Name what transitions
rules.instruction: List the properties a transition animates. transition-all also animates layout, size and color changes that were never meant to move.
rules.good: transition-colors on a hover fill, or transition: transform on an indicator.
rules.avoid: transition-all on a Button, which animates its width when the label changes.

rules.title: Time motion with tokens
rules.instruction: Take every transition and animation duration and easing from the motion tokens. Pick the duration by the size of what moves and the easing by whether it moves or only fades. A literal 150ms or ease-out drifts from its neighbours and cannot be tuned in one place.
rules.good: duration-(--v4-duration-fast) on a menu opening, or transition: width var(--v4-duration-moderate) var(--v4-ease-standard) on the sidebar.
rules.avoid: duration-200 ease-in-out on a sheet, or transition: height 180ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1) on a disclosure.
rules.exceptions: A reduced-motion snap to 0ms. Looping loaders keep their own timing and mark each line with v4-check-ignore.

rules.title: Docs must show the actual component
rules.instruction: Render each example using only the shipped component styles and its explicit layout wrappers. It must keep the same component appearance when rendered alone and inside the workbench. Hidden documentation selectors must not supply a missing component design.
rules.good: Docs prose styles scoped outside example frames.
rules.avoid: .docs button { border-radius: 8px }.
rules.exceptions: Named frame/layout constraints surrounding the example, never styling its internal controls.

rules.title: Errors name the failed task and recovery
rules.instruction: State what did not complete and the next available action beside the failed task. Preserve the draft or loaded records. Name a cause only when the host actually established it.
rules.good: Secret was not saved. Try again.
rules.avoid: Oops! Something went wrong.
rules.exceptions: Exact remote error details in a separate protected diagnostic area.

rules.title: Supporting text must add information
rules.instruction: For notifications and helper text, add the consequence or next step instead of repeating the title. When completion is already visible in the active task, prefer one accessible in-place confirmation. Repeating the same result through a toast, banner and inline live region interrupts the next task.
rules.good: One Token revoked confirmation with Clients using it can no longer authenticate.
rules.avoid: Token revoked followed by Your token has been revoked, then a toast announcing it again.
rules.exceptions: Keep the only accessible status announcement. Toasts may report useful off-screen completion or feedback without an inline home; retain durable retry or undo where needed.

rules.title: Protect exact values from editorial cleanup
rules.instruction: Keep commands, identifiers, keys and payloads exact through copying, formatting and translation. Prose edits must not change their case, quotes, punctuation or whitespace.
rules.good: Copying API_KEY=demo_value unchanged.
rules.avoid: Sentence-casing the key or curling shell quotes.
rules.exceptions: No secret-value rewrite; display masking is a separate presentation behavior.

rules.title: Pending preserves context
rules.instruction: When asynchronous work begins, show a named pending state where its result will appear. Keep the idle action label and outer box, expose busy state and block repeated activation while focus stays put. Reserve the known content shape, and keep useful rows and drafts visible so the person can see what is still outstanding.
rules.good: Save stays visible with an internal spinner while the retained rows show a named pending cue.
rules.avoid: A blank result area, or a Save button replaced by Processing your request... that shrinks the control.
rules.exceptions: Progress copy outside the control and a dedicated cancelable long-running task view. Do not impose a universal delay threshold or minimum loading duration.

rules.title: Announce completion only after completion
rules.instruction: Wait for the actual request or clipboard promise to fulfill before claiming success. A click, dialog dismissal or entered code is not a confirmed result. On rejection, keep the draft and offer a real recovery.
rules.good: Show Copied after writeText resolves.
rules.avoid: Showing Copied before the promise settles.
rules.exceptions: Explicitly modeled optimistic UI with rollback and a pending indicator, not a false success notification.

rules.title: Failed forms preserve recoverable work
rules.instruction: Keep entered values after a rejected submission. Identify the field or task that failed and associate its repair instruction with the actual control. The person should not need to reconstruct a valid draft.
rules.good: A failed save keeps the draft and associates the error.
rules.avoid: Closing and clearing the form on any response.
rules.exceptions: Sensitive inputs that an established security policy explicitly requires clearing, documented per field.

rules.title: Do not normalize identifiers or lose precision
rules.instruction: For adapters that display or edit numbers and identifiers, preserve the declared value type and units through edit and display. JavaScript numbers cannot represent every large integer exactly.
rules.good: An ID remains the string 000123.
rules.avoid: Number(id) producing 123.
rules.exceptions: Explicit format-only presentation with an unchanged underlying value.

rules.title: Destructive actions expose the consequence
rules.instruction: For irreversible changes, provide reversal, checking or confirmation that fits the risk, and name the object affected. Do not add confirmation to every harmless save.
rules.good: Revoke production token with the access consequence.
rules.avoid: A generic Are you sure? that hides scope.
rules.exceptions: Reversible operations with a real tested undo path.

rules.title: Navigation and selection are separate events
rules.instruction: Keep highlight, selected value and persisted result separate. State which supported event commits a choice and let the host own any subsequent write. Query changes and keyboard highlight must not silently save a value.
rules.good: Arrow keys move focus according to the chosen pattern without an unrelated network write.
rules.avoid: Opening a picker silently commits its first option.
rules.exceptions: Documented selection-follows-focus patterns where that behavior is intentional; network writes still require a deliberate contract.

rules.title: Preserve native semantics through composition
rules.instruction: Use a real button for an action and a real link for navigation. Custom asChild wrappers must spread required props and forward the DOM ref so focus, disabled state and event composition survive. Read each primitive's emitted attributes before changing its selectors, because not every active state uses data-state.
rules.good: asChild resolves to one actual link or button.
rules.avoid: An anchor wrapping a second interactive button, or a clickable div.
rules.exceptions: A documented composite widget using its APG pattern.

rules.title: Callbacks fire for the documented change
rules.instruction: For controlled inputs and compound controls, state whether reselecting the current value emits a callback and whether programmatic updates do. Test that contract instead of letting wrappers duplicate effects.
rules.good: One user commit yields the one documented event.
rules.avoid: Trigger and item handlers both saving the same selection.
rules.exceptions: Deliberately distinct preview and commit events with separate names and examples.

rules.title: Examples are inert and contain no live secrets
rules.instruction: Use synthetic values and local state in examples and trial tasks. Label a simulated operation where needed. Never put credentials into logs, diagnostics or captures, and never imply a local mutation reached a server.
rules.good: A fake secret and a local simulated rejection.
rules.avoid: A demo wired to the current organization's delete endpoint.
rules.exceptions: No live-write exemption in the workbench; separately authorized product tests belong elsewhere.

rules.title: The visible label is part of the accessible name
rules.instruction: For every control, make the spoken name contain the visible label text, and name icon-only actions by their purpose.
rules.good: Visible Save with the accessible name Save changes.
rules.avoid: Visible Save with aria-label="Confirm".
rules.exceptions: Symbolic labels whose meaning needs translation into words, documented in the component.

rules.title: Every supported action has a keyboard path
rules.instruction: For controls and composites, preserve the documented Radix and APG key behavior and test the whole task, including its escape paths.
rules.good: A row action reached by keyboard, or Tabs that select and focus the next trigger with the expected arrow key.
rules.avoid: A hover-only delete affordance.
rules.exceptions: Path-dependent drawing gestures with an equivalent keyboard operation; ordinary selection and deletion are never pointer-only exceptions.

rules.title: Focus remains visible and unobscured
rules.instruction: For every focusable example, keep a visible focus indicator and do not let sticky chrome completely cover the focused control. The Infisical target is fully visible focus where practical.
rules.good: Keyboard focus scrolls above the sticky footer.
rules.avoid: Setting outline: none with no replacement.
rules.exceptions: None for removing focus indication; WCAG's minimum coverage criterion is weaker than the proposed product target.

rules.title: Dialog focus follows the workflow
rules.instruction: For modal dialogs, move focus in, contain Tab navigation, close with Escape and restore focus to the opener or a logical successor.
rules.good: Deleting a row returns focus to the next row action.
rules.avoid: Focus falling to the document body.
rules.exceptions: A documented next-step workflow that intentionally moves focus elsewhere.

rules.title: Measure rendered contrast
rules.instruction: For text, meaningful control boundaries and icons, check the actual foreground and background combination in both themes, including opacity and portals. Use WCAG's applicable text thresholds and its 3:1 non-text threshold.
rules.good: A measured label over its composited surface.
rules.avoid: Declaring success from two uncomposited token values.
rules.exceptions: Criteria-defined exceptions such as inactive controls, not unlabelled low-emphasis active actions.

source.title: WCAG text contrast and non-text contrast

rules.title: Color never carries the only state cue
rules.instruction: For status, errors and selection, add a label, icon or structural cue so the information survives without its hue.
rules.good: An error icon plus associated error text.
rules.avoid: A red border as the only error cue.
rules.exceptions: Color samples whose purpose is to demonstrate color, with labels naming each sample.

rules.title: Reflow without losing operations
rules.instruction: For layouts and examples, keep text and actions reachable at 320 CSS px and at 200% text zoom. Let inherently two-dimensional tables and code scroll locally instead of clipping the whole page.
rules.good: Form actions wrap, and table actions stay inside the table's scroller.
rules.avoid: Hiding the only action at a breakpoint.
rules.exceptions: Criterion-defined two-dimensional content, never the surrounding page shell.

rules.title: Dense controls still have usable hit areas
rules.instruction: For pointer targets, meet WCAG's 24 by 24 CSS pixel target or its spacing provisions. Prefer a 44px hit area for coarse-pointer actions without forcing 44px desktop rows.
rules.good: A compact icon with a larger clickable box that overlaps nothing.
rules.avoid: Adjacent 12px targets.
rules.exceptions: WCAG's inline, equivalent, user-agent and essential cases; record which applies. The 44px preference is product guidance, not this AA criterion.

rules.title: Reduced motion keeps meaning
rules.instruction: For animation and loaders, remove nonessential movement when the person asks for reduced motion, and keep the state and completion cues.
rules.good: A stable busy label or a restrained opacity cue.
rules.avoid: Disabling the only loading cue, or keeping a large slide because it is CSS-only.
rules.exceptions: Essential motion under the criterion; identify the mechanism. This criterion is AAA, while the product can adopt it voluntarily.

rules.title: Let authentication tools do their job
rules.instruction: For password, token and one-time code entry, allow paste and the applicable autocomplete, and keep the exact value. Do not force manual transcription as a styling or validation shortcut.
rules.good: Pasting a whole OTP fills its complete value.
rules.avoid: A split input that accepts only the first pasted digit.
rules.exceptions: Criteria-defined alternative mechanisms, explicitly documented. Do not infer that every arbitrary secret field should autofill credentials.

rules.title: Give each component one identity
rules.instruction: For the registry and docs, keep item names unique and resolve docs and example metadata from the existing registry and catalog instead of a parallel handwritten list.
rules.good: One item generates navigation and the agent index.
rules.avoid: Three lists with different component counts.
rules.exceptions: Noninstallable foundation pages explicitly typed as documentation.

rules.title: Declare the whole install contract
rules.instruction: For local registry output, include the required npm dependencies, registry dependencies, targets, styles and support files, then test installation into a clean consumer.
rules.good: A local install includes its helper and preserves consumer instructions.
rules.avoid: Registry JSON that builds but imports a missing package.
rules.exceptions: Explicitly required host peers listed and checked before install, not hidden assumptions.

rules.title: State support before the first example
rules.instruction: On agent component pages, put the actual import, runtime compatibility, support status and known limits before long examples, so an agent does not treat a planned component as usable.
rules.good: Planned; not yet available in this React 19 foundation.
rules.avoid: A working-looking import for the same item.
rules.exceptions: Conceptual pages with no import, explicitly typed as conceptual.

rules.title: Keep the agent entry point short
rules.instruction: In the Infisical UI skill, give task triggers, reading order, component lookup and the real checks, then link to detail. Do not repeat every component rule inside it.
rules.good: An entry point linking to the affected component pages.
rules.avoid: A giant skill that loads every page on every task.
rules.exceptions: No arbitrary universal line limit; set the local budget from observed usefulness.

rules.title: Examples prove supported APIs
rules.instruction: In docs, compile, render and display the same example module against current exports. Do not keep a parallel snippet that drops required imports, invents props or changes fixture behavior. An attractive snippet is not evidence that the API exists.
rules.good: One imported example module rendered and shown as its raw source.
rules.avoid: A separate handwritten code block with an unsupported prop, or a visual textarea presented as a complete editor.
rules.exceptions: Explicitly labeled pseudocode outside copyable usage examples.

rules.title: Fix repeated gaps in the foundation
rules.instruction: When an agent using v4 in its allowed workbench finds a required style or state missing, record the gap and improve the component or token once. Do not hide the gap with caller restyling or another local wrapper.
rules.good: Add and document a justified reusable variant.
rules.avoid: Two examples independently overriding padding, color and focus rings.
rules.exceptions: Layout wrappers, not visual overrides; one-off specimen experiments explicitly marked noncanonical.

rules.title: Do not fabricate operational metrics
rules.instruction: Show measured operational values immediately with their real period, or label synthetic fixtures as example data. Count-up figures and tickers show invented intermediate values that people can misread. Do not invent customer counts, percentage lifts or trend arrows to populate a page.
rules.good: 12 synchronized versions from the actual result on first paint, or a chart labelled Example data.
rules.avoid: A number animating through false values, made-up uptime or a trend with no measured comparison.

rules.title: Do not invent activity or urgency
rules.instruction: Show an activity row only when a real event or explicitly synthetic fixture produced it. Explain an empty feed instead of filling it with fabricated recent actions or urgency.
rules.good: No activity yet, with the action that creates the first event.
rules.avoid: Fake people approving requests moments ago or an invented last-sync timestamp.

rules.title: Start with the current task
rules.instruction: When the task compares resources, lead with the resources, relevant action and shared reading edge. Change the layout when content or interaction changes. Centered welcomes, large metric tiles and repeated icon-title-copy-action blocks can push the actual work below the first viewport.
rules.good: A connection list with aligned fields, a filter and Add connection visible before scrolling.
rules.avoid: A centered promotional hero followed by equal big-number tiles above the connection list.
rules.exceptions: Empty states, authentication and deliberate brand or layout specimens may center. There is no universal card-count limit or required layout variation.

rules.title: Status must describe a real state
rules.instruction: When status affects a task, place the meaningful exception with its subject using the owned badge slot. Its value must come from a defined state with a consequence. Keep routine dates, owners and descriptive metadata quiet so equal chips do not hide the exception.
rules.good: Expired beside a credential that no longer authenticates.
rules.avoid: A decorative New badge above a title or badge strips for every owner, date and category.
rules.exceptions: Keep useful Count, supported status dots and independent statuses the task needs. There is no universal one-badge limit.

rules.title: Give an icon a job
rules.instruction: Use icons to identify a recognizable action, object or status. Name every icon-only action. When an actor or review state matters to relying on generated content, state it truthfully in words; a sparkle or wand cannot establish who produced or checked it.
rules.good: A named Copy value action, or a truthful review state beside content when the task requires it.
rules.avoid: Repeated icon-per-heading decoration or a sparkle used as the only review-state cue.
rules.exceptions: Owned Media and Tile exports and explicit icon specimens keep their semantic role; do not ban canonical APIs.

rules.title: Draw icons from the v4 set first
rules.instruction: Render icons with the v4 Icon component and one of the 52 v4 icon names. Use a Lucide icon (Icon icon={...} or a direct lucide-react import) only for a glyph the set lacks, sized by the size tokens at stroke-icon (1.7). Do not import another icon library or hand-draw SVG icons.
rules.good: <Icon name="chev-down" /> inside a Select trigger, sized by --v4-size-icon; <Icon icon={ArrowUpDown} /> for an unsorted column, which the set lacks.
rules.avoid: A Lucide ChevronDown where the set has chev-down, an import from react-icons or @radix-ui/react-icons, or an inline <svg> path drawn by hand.

rules.title: Every control must perform its advertised action
rules.instruction: Every enabled control must perform its named operation, change the demonstrated model or navigate to a real destination. A notification alone cannot stand in for Save, Test connection, Undo or Download. Keep unavailable controls disabled with an accessible reason.
rules.good: A preview Save changes action updates a local fixture and announces its result.
rules.avoid: A search field that never filters, href="#" links that jump to the top, or a decorative kebab menu.

rules.title: Truncate presentation, preserve the value
rules.instruction: Keep stored and copied identifiers byte-for-byte intact. A truncated display needs a keyboard-accessible route to the full value, such as a Copy action or details view. A native hover title alone is insufficient. Use middle truncation when both ends identify the object.
rules.good: A labeled Copy full path action beside the shortened path, preserving the original value.
rules.avoid: An ellipsis copied as part of a token, or a shortened value that keyboard users cannot recover.

rules.title: Avoid ambient effects in task interfaces
rules.instruction: When grouping a task or distinguishing status, use the owned surface, text and supported state treatment. Keep opaque content surfaces readable. Avoid caller-created colored side rails, gradient headings, glass backdrops, ambient glows, decorative pulses and staggered entrances because they compete with the task and change contrast. Keep corners square and preserve the canonical shared lime Button material; do not add shadows or local material replicas.
rules.good: An opaque scoped menu and a short disclosure transition tied to opening.
rules.avoid: A glowing settings card, glass panel or colored rail added only for decoration.
rules.exceptions: The approved shared Button material and deliberate material or motion specimens retain their documented treatment.

rules.title: Depth comes from two shadow tokens
rules.instruction: Give an overlay shadow-pop and an inset surface shadow-raised. Do not add other Tailwind shadows, arbitrary shadows or backdrop blur; focus, selection and errors use borders, outlines and color.
rules.good: A menu panel with shadow-pop on an opaque popover surface.
rules.avoid: shadow-md on one menu, shadow-lg on another and backdrop-blur-xs behind a dialog.

rules.title: Apply research to the actual task
rules.instruction: Read the current component decision and the pinned product brief before importing an external recommendation. Distinguish design opinion from usability guidance and accessibility criteria. Preserve the approved identity. Explain a missing capability with source evidence instead of adding a fashionable replacement.
rules.good: A compact table with scoped selection because the task compares resources, retaining the existing fonts and shared Button.
rules.avoid: Banning a font or accent because an article calls it an AI tell, or applying marketing-page entrance effects to every operational row.

rules.title: Separate a check from its result
rules.instruction: Describe each rule with a real condition, a supported construction, a concrete misuse, its consequence and how it is assessed. Treat each verification criterion as work to perform. Record the actual command or browser scenario, its result and the remaining limits before calling the criterion executed. Source links, rule counts, authored good and bad pairs and generated coverage show traceability, not usability, accessibility or runtime success.
rules.good: Report that a rejected save retained its draft in the named runtime test, while mobile browser verification remains unrun.
rules.avoid: A Verified label inferred from a source citation or generated Markdown, or a regex presented as a hierarchy checker.
rules.exceptions: Review-only rules still need a concrete counterexample; they need no pretend linter.

rules.title: Show the interface inside the specimen
rules.instruction: Keep preview content to the demonstrated interface, meaningful helper text, synthetic-data or security disclosures and actual state feedback. Put inspection coaching in the guide. Use meaningful synthetic media when it teaches the task; unrelated stock images, mascots and arbitrary image-icon blocks add no useful information.
rules.good: A labeled field and truthful local save result, with synthetic data disclosed. A media specimen has useful alt text and a fallback.
rules.avoid: Try clicking Save to see what happens, slogans above obvious actions or a decorative image used only to fill space.
rules.exceptions: Explicit media and aspect-ratio specimens may use safe placeholders to demonstrate the supported shape. Never use private documents, real customers or secrets.

rules.title: Keep required decisions visible
rules.instruction: Disclose supplementary information on demand. Keep a warning, blocking error, required input and the consequence of a destructive action visible before the decision that depends on it. Do not move essential content into a tooltip or collapsed help region merely to make a page look cleaner.
rules.good: A visible revoke consequence before confirmation and an optional details disclosure for the request metadata.
rules.avoid: Hiding a save failure or required constraint inside an unopened accordion.

rules.title: Show progress the host can establish
rules.instruction: Use determinate progress only when the host knows completed work and a meaningful total, and expose the actual value and range with an accessible name. Otherwise show an indeterminate pending state and the operation name. Announce a meaningful completion or failure without inventing elapsed time, percentages or remaining duration.
rules.good: 18 of 30 resources checked, or Checking resources when the total is unknown.
rules.avoid: A timer that increments to 95 percent while the host reports no measurable progress.
rules.exceptions: A static illustration explicitly presented as non-status content.

rules.title: Pad overlay sections evenly
rules.instruction: Dialog, AlertDialog and Sheet headers, bodies and footers pad all four sides by the one overlay pad (space-16 for dialogs, the overlay inset for sheets). Sections stack with the content gap and carry no margins.
rules.good: A dialog footer padded 16px on every side, the same as the header and body.
rules.avoid: A footer padded 12px 16px, or a header with extra end padding beyond the close button slot.
rules.exceptions: The header's end padding that reserves the close button slot.

rules.title: Pressing never moves the control box
rules.instruction: A pressed button, toggle or segment keeps its border, fill, size and position. The press shows on the label: the text and icons inside [data-press] scale to 0.97 on duration-fast with ease-press and spring back on release, and the pressed fill stays on the box. With reduced motion only the fill changes.
rules.good: An icon-only button whose glyph shrinks slightly while its square stays put.
rules.avoid: translate: 0 1px or scale(0.98) on the button on :active.
rules.exceptions: Drag handles and sliders that move by design.

rules.title: Fade only the edge that has more
rules.instruction: Page and inset scrollers never fade; component scrollers do. Every component scroll area (ScrollArea, menus and lists, CommandMenu, the Sidebar nav, Table, DataGrid, Code, FileTree, Json, and the Sheet and Dialog bodies) carries data-scroll-fade on the element that scrolls. The AppInset island and any other page-level scroller scroll with crisp edges, so the island's top edge under the TopBar band stays solid. The shared watcher in lib/scroll-edges.ts marks each edge that has more content past it, and v4.css masks only that edge by size-scroll-fade (16px). An area that does not scroll shows no fade. ScrollArea takes edgeBehavior fade (default), border or none.
rules.good: A long menu whose bottom edge fades until the last row is scrolled into view, then fades at the top instead.
rules.avoid: A one-off mask-image or scroll-timeline fade on a single component, a fade on an area that does not scroll, or a fade on the AppInset that blurs the island's top edge.
rules.exceptions: Inputs and scroll containers the person drags or that host their own virtualized edge treatment, marked with v4-check-ignore scroll-fade and a reason.

rules.title: Space menus from one panel padding
rules.instruction: Every menu-like popover pads all four sides by one token, --v4-menu-pad. Rows, labels, theme and user rows carry no outer margin and fill the inset, so hover and highlight blocks never touch the panel edge. A separator is a full-width 1px rule drawn the same pad below the previous row and above the next one.
rules.good: The first row sits 3px from the panel top, the last row 3px from the bottom, and each rule sits 3px from the rows on both sides.
rules.avoid: A separator with margin: 4px 0, a footer row with a negative inline margin, or a row that runs flush to the panel edge.
rules.exceptions: Auto margins inside a row that push trailing content to the end are layout, not outer spacing.

rules.title: Separate labels without decorative dots
rules.instruction: In authored UI labels and prose, use clear wording or separate text and layout instead of middle-dot or bullet separators. Decorative dots add punctuation without explaining how the details relate.
rules.good: Primary, alias of default. Put an owner and date in separate labeled fields when their relationship needs context.
rules.avoid: Primary · alias of default, or dot · synthetic requests used as display labels.
rules.exceptions: Preserve exact payloads, filenames, versions, paths, quotations and user-entered values. Semantic list markers, supported status dots and Chart dot indicator APIs are not decorative separators.

rules.title: A crumb's name navigates; its chevron switches
rules.instruction: Give every switcher crumb (organization, project, environment and similar) two targets. The name goes to that level's page through link (a typed route built with linkOptions), href or onNavigate; the chevron is its own button, named for its purpose such as Switch project, and is what opens the Switcher. Only when a level has no page of its own, or is the current page, does the whole segment (media, name and chevron) become one button that opens the Switcher. A crumb with neither a page nor a switcher is plain text.
rules.good: Acme Corp links to the organization home and its chevron opens Switch organization; Production has no page, so its name and its chevron both open Switch environment.
rules.avoid: A crumb whose name opens the switcher popover although the level has a page, or a name that looks like a link and does nothing.
rules.exceptions: None: every crumb is a link to its page, a trigger for its switcher, or plain text.

rules.title: Separate crumbs with the vertical divider
rules.instruction: Let Breadcrumb (or BreadcrumbSeparator) draw the separator between crumbs: a 1px vertical divider in crumb-divider, size-crumb-divider tall, with space-crumb-divider on each side between the line and the neighboring crumb's ground. Never type a slash or another character between crumbs.
rules.good: Acme Corp | payments-api | Production, with every divider drawn by the component from tokens.
rules.avoid: A literal / between crumbs, a chevron glyph used as a separator, or a divider drawn with raw sizes and colors.
rules.exceptions: Literal paths and values, such as a secret path shown in a code font, keep their slashes.

rules.title: Use complete component recipes
rules.instruction: Choose the owned type, control, row or container recipe as a unit. Size includes border-inclusive height, text role, icon box, gap, insets and nested action space. Use layout wrappers for relationships between components. A missing shared relationship is a component issue, not permission for a caller font, padding or radius patch.
rules.good: A field and its supporting action consume their supported sizes and align without caller overrides.
rules.avoid: A succession of local text-size, padding and translate corrections to make one specimen resemble its neighbor.

rules.title: Size with tokens, not arbitrary values
rules.instruction: Use the component's size recipe or a v4 size or space token. An arbitrary Tailwind value such as max-w-[440px] or ring-[3px] creates a one-off measurement no other component shares.
rules.good: max-w-md on a dialog, or the focus ring width from the shared control recipe.
rules.avoid: max-w-[440px], rounded-[2px] or ring-[3px] written into a component.

rules.title: Fit actions inside their host
rules.instruction: A copy, reveal, clear or menu action nested in a control consumes the host action slot. Keep its target reachable without forcing the host to adopt a standalone Button height. Supported host sizes must remain distinct, and adding an optional capability must not change one-line density accidentally.
rules.good: Small and medium snippets stay distinct with Copy present, and revealing a secret does not enlarge its one-line field.
rules.avoid: A default standalone action plus vertical padding that makes every advertised host size the same height.

rules.title: Badges in control rows take the control height
rules.instruction: A badge that shares a row or grid track with regular-height controls takes the control height. Use the Badge control size that matches its neighbors: control-sm beside the default 32px Input, Select and Button, control-md beside md and control-lg beside lg. Keep the compact sm and md badges for status inside text, table cells and a field's nested slot.
rules.good: FieldMapping's source Badge at control-sm beside a 32px Input, with the arrow centered on the same height.
rules.avoid: A 20px Badge floating in a 32px form row, or a page-local span copying the input's height, padding and border.

detect.how: Measure rows that mix a Badge with an Input, Select or Button. Whether two elements share a row depends on the rendered grid or flex layout, not on JSX nesting, so a static check would miss grid tracks and flag nested slots.

rules.title: Keep title rank across container treatments
rules.instruction: A plain section, framed Card and settings task keep the same title role when they express the same hierarchy. Border, tint and framing do not select a new font size, uppercase treatment or semantic level. Align named header, body and footer content edges through the owning component.
rules.good: The same section title keeps its type role when its frame changes.
rules.avoid: A framed Card silently converts a section title into tiny uppercase metadata while a plain variant uses a heading.

rules.title: Disable blocked actions, do not hide them
rules.instruction: When the person may not take an action, keep its control visible and disabled, with a reason in its title or nearby text. Never remove it, especially when removal shifts the layout. Gate each action only by its own permission: a person who may view a secret may copy it while it is still masked.
rules.good: A disabled Reveal and Copy in SensitiveEditor for someone without view access, in the same place as for someone with it.
rules.avoid: Dropping Copy until the value is revealed, or removing Replace for a read-only person so the row reflows.

rules.title: A disabled Button says why through disabledReason
rules.instruction: To explain why a Button is unavailable, pass the reason as disabledReason. It keeps the Button focusable with aria-disabled, shows the reason in its own tooltip on hover and keyboard focus and carries it as the accessible description. Never put a natively disabled Button inside a Tooltip or TooltipTrigger, and never wrap it in a span to catch the pointer: a natively disabled button takes no pointer or focus events, so without the span hover never opens the tooltip, and with it keyboard users still never reach the reason.
rules.good: Tooltip content={reason ? undefined : "Export CSV"} around Button disabledReason={reason}, which shows the label while the action is enabled and the reason while it is blocked.
rules.avoid: A Tooltip saying Only admins can export around a span holding Button disabled, which hover can open but Tab never reaches.
rules.exceptions: A Button disabled only while its own request is pending uses loading instead. The check reads Buttons written directly inside a Tooltip or TooltipTrigger; a Button rendered by a child component is reviewed by hand.

rules.title: Tooltips are pass-through; hovered content uses HoverCard
rules.instruction: A tooltip is a short label the pointer passes through: it cannot be hovered into or text-selected, it closes as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger, and it opens on keyboard focus but never on focus a closing overlay returns. Never put a link, button, input, copy action or click handler inside Tooltip content or TooltipContent. Use HoverCard for content meant to be read at length, selected or copied, and Popover when it holds actions.
rules.good: Tooltip content="Remove from favorites" on an icon Button, and a HoverCard listing the invisible characters a secret value contains so their code points can be selected.
rules.avoid: A Tooltip whose content holds a Docs link or a Copy button, or a long value a person is expected to hover into and copy.
rules.exceptions: The check reads Tooltip content props and TooltipContent bodies in the same file. A long or copyable value with no interactive element is reviewed by hand.

rules.title: Mono is for machine values, names stay in the sans
rules.instruction: Set Geist Mono only on machine-readable values a person copies or compares character by character: secret keys, IDs and UUIDs, hashes, fingerprints, serials, IPs and hosts, paths, env var names, code and CLI snippets and key IDs, and optionally tabular numbers whose digits must align. Names people chose stay in the Archivo sans: project, organization, environment display name, role, group, identity (person, machine or agent), user, folder, KMS key, certificate common name and app connection names, and every crumb, switcher option, title and label built from them. A slug is an identifier the CLI, API and URLs use, so it takes mono where it is shown or edited as the slug (a slug field, a slug column, an inline code reference), but never stands in for the display name, even when the two match. Never set a font family on html, body, V4Scope, AppShell or a theme, and set mono in a page only through a primitive's mono prop or the mono type role tokens on a machine value; DataTable primary is sans and a column opts into mono with mono.
rules.good: The top bar's project crumb and switcher options and the project's PageHeader title in the sans, beside a secret key column with mono and an environment slug Input with mono.
rules.avoid: A project, identity or folder name passed with mono to a crumb, Switcher option, PageHeader or Item, or a page stylesheet that sets a name class in the mono family.
rules.exceptions: The check reads mono on a JSX element or option object whose title, label or text reads an entity's .name. It cannot see a name passed through a local variable, mono set by a page stylesheet class, a conditional mono expression or a DataTable column whose render reads a name; those are reviewed by hand.

rules.title: Tab tracks and their triggers share one width
rules.instruction: Tabs and ToggleGroup take one width prop that sizes the track and its triggers together. width="full" stretches the track to its container and every trigger to an equal share of it; the default width="content" fits the track to its triggers. Never set a width, flex or grow on a tab list, track or trigger yourself.
rules.good: A segmented Tabs with width="full" in a narrow sidebar, where both segments split the track evenly, and a content-width segmented Tabs in a sheet that ends after its last tab.
rules.avoid: A tint track that spans the whole sheet while its three tabs sit at the start at their label widths, leaving an empty stretch of track after them.
rules.exceptions: The check reads className strings and CSS rules that select a tab, tab list, toggle group or toggle item by role or data-slot; a page class that reaches the parts another way is reviewed by hand.

rules.title: Triggers start-align their value
rules.instruction: Every trigger that shows a value and a chevron (Select, Combobox, MultiSelect, and a Button that opens a menu, popover or picker) puts its label at the start, truncates it, and puts the chevron at the end. A Button acting as that trigger passes layout="trigger", which draws the chevron and takes SelectTrigger's insets; never center the value or add a chevron to a plain Button.
rules.good: Button variant="outline" layout="trigger" at a fixed width inside a PopoverTrigger, showing Production at the start and the chevron at the end, beside a Select of the same width.
rules.avoid: Button iconRight="chev-down" at a fixed width, which centers Production and its chevron in the middle of the box.
rules.exceptions: Icon-only chevron Buttons have no label to align. The check reads Buttons written inside a PopoverTrigger or DropdownMenuTrigger in the same file; a trigger Button rendered by a child component is reviewed by hand.

rules.title: Bulk selection uses the floating action bar
rules.instruction: When rows are selected, show the count, Clear and the bulk actions in the FloatingActionBar overlay, never in an inline bar above or below the list. Selecting or clearing rows must not move any content. The bar is fixed to the bottom center of the window on every page, crossing the sidebar if it must; pass it to DataTable's actionBar when a DataTable holds the selection, and never position it yourself. It pads the page's scroll area while it shows, so the last rows and the pagination scroll clear of it.
rules.good: Selecting three secrets raises the floating action bar at the bottom center of the window with the count, Clear and the bulk actions, the table stays where it was, and scrolling to the end shows the pagination above the bar.
rules.avoid: An inline '3 selected, Clear selection, Bulk actions' row that pushes the table down when the first row is selected.

detect.how: Select a row and check that nothing above or below the list moves, that the bar sits at the bottom center of the window, and that the pagination scrolls clear of it.

rules.title: One translucent hover color
rules.instruction: Every neutral hover ground uses var(--v4-hover) and every pressed ground var(--v4-press): sidebar rows and tools, table, list, tree and grid rows, menu and listbox rows, segments, ghost and outline actions and tiles. Both are translucent ink (color-mix(in oklab, ink hover-mix, transparent)), so they land on whatever ground is underneath, shift it darker in light schemes and brighter in dark ones and need no per-theme value. Tune strength only through hover-mix and press-mix. Where the fill must be opaque, such as a pinned cell or a ring that cuts out a dot, mix ink at var(--v4-hover-mix) into that ground with color-mix in srgb, which matches how the overlay composites. Current and selected states keep their own, stronger grounds.
rules.good: Background var(--v4-hover) on a hovered sidebar row, table row or menu row, and color-mix(in srgb, var(--v4-ink) var(--v4-hover-mix), var(--v4-surface)) on a pinned actions cell of a hovered row.
rules.avoid: A hovered row painted var(--v4-tint), a per-theme flat hover color such as the old sidebar-hover, or an opaque hover that hides the ground underneath.
rules.exceptions: The check reads :hover rules that paint their own element; a hovered element that keeps a pressed, current or selected state keeps that state's ground, and pseudo-element handles such as a resize line are not grounds.

rules.title: Only links take the pointer cursor
rules.instruction: Styled controls keep the default cursor, even when one renders an anchor: Button in every variant except link, Toggle and ToggleGroup, Select, Combobox and MultiSelect triggers, menu, Switcher and Sidebar rows, Tabs, crumb switcher triggers and chevrons, row actions, nav sheet rows, Checkbox, Radio and Switch. Their hover and press grounds already show they act. Only links take cursor: pointer: text anchors, RowLink and CardLink with the row or card they cover, crumb names that navigate, the link Button variant, and unstyled text buttons that read as links, such as a List title or a toast action.
rules.good: An outline Export Button with the arrow cursor and its hover ground, beside a docs link in body text that shows the pointer.
rules.avoid: cursor: pointer on a Select trigger, a Sidebar row or a Button that renders an anchor, or a cursor-pointer class added so a control feels clickable.
rules.exceptions: A selector that names a link (a, [href], :any-link, or link in a class or attribute name) passes. An unstyled text button that reads as a link, or a DataTable row that opens its record like a RowLink row, keeps the pointer and marks the rule with v4-check-ignore cursor-pointer and that reason.

rules.title: No left accent bars
rules.instruction: Never mark a row, card, Alert, list item or current state with a colored stripe or tinted edge on its left (or inline-start) side, even where main uses one. Carry the state with a translucent tint over the whole row or surface, a labeled Badge, an icon with text, or weight, so the meaning reads without color.
rules.good: A batch-edited secret row with a translucent ok tint across the row and a Modified badge beside its name; a deleted one with a bad tint and a Deleted badge.
rules.avoid: A 2px green or red inset line down the first cell, a colored left border on an Alert or callout, or a tinted left edge on the current nav item.
rules.exceptions: Structure is not an accent: tree hierarchy guides, timeline connectors and column or pane dividers drawn in line or line-soft stay.

rules.title: Row actions are persistent, in the actions tail
rules.instruction: Put row-level actions in the table's actions tail, visible on every row at rest: DataTable rowActions, or TableActionsCell with RowActions in a native Table. Show at most three inline icon actions (Button icon-row, each with a tooltip and an accessible name that includes the row), then the More menu for everything else. A blocked action stays visible and disabled with its reason. Nothing a hover or focus shows may change a cell's width or the row's layout.
rules.good: A secret row with Reminder, Edit value and Copy secret icons and a More menu in the actions tail that keeps one width on every row, hovered or not.
rules.avoid: Copy and More icons that appear inside the value cell on hover and push its content aside, or indicator marks that swap out for actions.
rules.exceptions: A same-size glyph swap inside a fixed box, such as a folder glyph that turns into a chevron, keeps the layout still. Mark it with v4-check-ignore and the reason.

rules.title: Destructive row actions go last in the More menu
rules.instruction: Destructive row actions (Delete, Remove, Revoke, Disable and similar irreversible or access-removing actions) never appear in rowActions.inline or RowActions inline. They appear in the More menu as its last item, after a separator if the menu has other items, using the destructive menu item variant (DropdownMenuItem variant destructive). A row whose only action is destructive still uses More, so More is the single action in the actions tail.
rules.good: A members table with Edit user inline and a More menu that ends with a separator and a destructive Remove user item; a service token row whose only action is Delete token shows More alone.
rules.avoid: A trash or Remove user icon in the inline actions beside Edit and Copy, or a Delete item placed above other items in the More menu.

rules.title: Rows that navigate use RowLink
rules.instruction: When activating a table row goes to another page, put RowLink in the primary cell with the record's route. It stretches over the row, keeps its chevron and gives the row a real href. Never navigate from onRowActivate with a router call (navigate, router.navigate or a helper such as useGo), and never set RowLink and onRowActivate on the same table.
rules.good: A members table whose name cell is a RowLink to the member's page, so the row opens in a new tab on a modified click and its link can be copied.
rules.avoid: onRowActivate={(row) => go(links.member(row.id))} over plain text in the name cell, or a certificates table that sets a RowLink and an onRowActivate that navigates to the same page.
rules.exceptions: The check reads the inline handler and any function it calls that is defined in the same file. A handler imported from another module is not followed, so review those by hand.

rules.title: Pagination sits in the table frame, compact
rules.instruction: Pass a paged DataTable's Pagination through its pagination slot with variant="compact", so it renders in the frame's foot below the rows and stays in view while the table scrolls. Never render Pagination as a sibling after the table, and never put the numbered variant in the slot. A helper that builds the pagination returns that compact node for the slot.
rules.good: A roles list whose DataTable gets pagination={<Pagination variant="compact" ... />}, with the range and arrows inside the frame under the last row.
rules.avoid: A Stack holding the DataTable and then {list.pagination}, a numbered Pagination drawn below the frame.
rules.exceptions: A grid of cards or another collection that is not a DataTable renders its own Pagination below it. A slot value built in a variable or helper is not read, so check its variant by hand.

rules.title: Action results go to a toast
rules.instruction: Report the result of an action (copied, saved, deleted, moved, uploaded, and every failure) with a toast from @infisical/sonner. The toast region is a live region, so the result is announced without a separate role="status" line. A DataTable's persistentStatus, a List or DataGrid footer and a toolbar status line hold only state that must stay visible while the person works, such as Showing 5 of 120 after filter.
rules.good: Copy secret name on a secrets row calls toast("Copied the name hello."), and the table footer keeps showing the row counts.
rules.avoid: A notice state set by row actions and rendered in the table footer, so Copied the name hello. replaces the counts bottom left and nothing announces it unless a hidden role="status" paragraph repeats it.
rules.exceptions: Keep a result in place only when it must outlive a toast, such as a bulk job's progress that the person reads while it runs; say why in the persistentStatus value's owner. State set through a helper or a prop from another file is not traced, so check those by hand.

rules.title: Rows that open a sheet use onRowActivate and a named button
rules.instruction: When activating a row opens the record in a Sheet or Dialog on the same page, pass onRowActivate and render the primary cell's name as a quiet link Button, variant="link" with underline="hover", that runs the same handler. The name reads as plain text at rest and underlines on hover and keyboard focus, and keyboard and screen reader users meet a named control. That cell is not a RowLink, so no chevron is drawn: a chevron says the row leaves the page. Add no inline Open or chevron action for the same sheet.
rules.good: A findings table whose row opens the finding's sheet on click or Enter, with the finding's name as a quiet link Button that underlines on hover in the primary cell and More alone in the actions tail.
rules.avoid: A chevron button column that opens the sheet, an inline Open action that repeats the row's own target, or a RowLink with its chevron on a row that never leaves the page.

detect.how: Open a row by click, by Enter and by its name button. All three open the same sheet, and the row shows no chevron and no Open action.

rules.exceptions: A sheet that is addressable by URL may use a RowLink to that URL in the primary cell; pass chevron={false} there, since the person stays on the page.

rules.title: Hand-built rows with actions take the row context menu
rules.instruction: A hand-built native Table row that shows RowActions or a TableActionsCell wraps itself in RowContextMenu, passing the same label, inline actions, menu and menuDisabledReason it passes RowActions. Right-click, Shift+F10 and the Menu key then open the row's actions exactly as on a DataTable row with rowActions.
rules.good: A secrets overview environment row wrapped in RowContextMenu with Copy value and Edit inline and the same More items, so right-clicking it lists those actions with Delete last.
rules.avoid: A nested Table row with RowActions in its actions tail and no RowContextMenu, so right-clicking it opens the browser's menu.
rules.exceptions: A row assigned to a variable counts as wrapped when that variable sits inside a RowContextMenu in the same file. A row built in one file and wrapped in another is flagged, so wrap it where it is built.

rules.title: Detail-page facts cards are compact
rules.instruction: The facts card on a detail page, the DetailLayout sidecar or the details Card that heads a record page, renders its DataList with density="compact" and pairs short values with span half. A DataList inside a Sheet or Dialog keeps the default density.
rules.good: A group detail sidecar whose Details card lists Name, Slug, Role and Created as compact 32px rows, with Created and Updated paired on one row.
rules.avoid: One detail page with a compact facts card and the next with default-density rows that spread the same facts twice as tall.

detect.how: Open each record detail page and check its facts card uses compact density, while DataLists in sheets keep the default.

rules.title: Resource rows inline their one most-used action
rules.instruction: On a table of resources, inline the single most-used non-destructive action for that resource, such as Edit, Rotate or View logs, then More for everything else. A resource with no clearly most-used action shows More alone. Never inline an action that repeats the row's own target, and keep destructive actions in More (rule/row-actions-destructive-in-more).
rules.good: A roles table with Edit role inline and Duplicate, Export and Delete in More, and a KMS keys table with More alone because no key action dominates.
rules.avoid: Edit, Duplicate and Copy ID inline on every row of a resource list, or an inline Open or Access project action beside a row that already opens it.

detect.how: For each resource list, name the action people use most. It is the only inline action, it is not destructive and it does not repeat the row's target.

rules.title: List pages search and filter with FilterBar
rules.instruction: A full list page puts its search and filters in FilterBar: the search Input in its search slot, filter fields in fields, and list tools such as Columns, Export or one always-used Select in actions. A page with nothing to filter still uses FilterBar with no fields, which draws search and actions without Add filter. A search box with an icon-only filter menu is only for search inside a Card header.
rules.good: A KMS keys page with FilterBar holding the key search, no Add filter and a usage Select in actions, the same shape as the certificates inventory.
rules.avoid: A bare Input above one list page, an Input and a Select row on the next and a toolbar with an icon-only filter menu on a third.

detect.how: Compare the toolbar above each full list page: every one is a FilterBar, and only search inside a Card header uses the compact toolbar.

rules.title: Tables inside cards are DataTables
rules.instruction: A table inside a Card or SettingsCard on a page is a DataTable, which embeds frameless on the card's inset and brings sorting, loading rows and the empty state. The native Table is reserved for the secrets overview matrix and for tables inside a Dialog, Sheet or Popover, where the Table contract already allows it.
rules.good: A secret approval's Changes and Reviewers cards each holding an embedded DataTable with its own empty state.
rules.avoid: A native Table with hand-written rows inside a framed Card on a detail page, beside another card that uses DataTable for the same kind of list.
rules.exceptions: A chart legend laid out as a table beside its chart is not a list of records; keep it a native Table and mark it with v4-check-ignore raw-table-in-card and that reason.

rules.title: Build v4 links through the path helpers
rules.instruction: Never write the /v4 prefix as a literal in pages/v4 or components/v4: not in to= or href=, navigate or redirect, startsWith checks or regular expressions. Build every v4 link through the v4 link helpers in pages/v4/links.ts (orgHref, useGo) and the other modules in the check's v4PathModules list. The resolver lives in src/helpers/v4Bridge.ts, so moving v4 to the root at launch changes those modules and the route definitions only.
rules.good: <RowLink href={accessLinks.orgMember(orgId, id)}>, with the /v4/organizations prefix spelled once inside access/links.ts.
rules.avoid: href={`/v4/organizations/${orgId}/members/${id}`} in a page, or pathname.startsWith("/v4") in a component.
rules.exceptions: Route definition files (route.tsx, src/routes.ts and pages/v4/routes.ts) and the modules in the check's v4PathModules list may spell the prefix. A route ID passed as a from: value (useParams, useSearch, useRouteContext, useLoaderData) or to getRouteApi is exempt, because TanStack type-checks it and a root move fails the build at every stale one. Any other line that must spell it, such as code that runs before the router exists, takes v4-check-ignore v4-path-literal with the reason.

rules.title: Skeleton when the shape is known, Loader when it is not
rules.instruction: Inside a page that has rendered, when the shape of the content being loaded is known or measurable, show Skeleton shapes that match the loaded state at the same size. Use a Loader only when the shape is unknown. A whole page that is still loading takes the page loader instead (rule/page-loading).
rules.good: Reloading connections shows two skeleton rows shaped like the Vercel and GitHub rows.
rules.avoid: A centered spinner over a list whose rows are already known.

rules.title: Page loader for pages, Skeleton for regions, loading rows for tables
rules.instruction: Pick the loading treatment by what is waiting. While a whole page or its lazy chunk loads and none of it is on screen yet (a route or Suspense boundary around a page, a detail page's first fetch), fill the page body with the page loader, Loader size page, labeled with the page it loads. Once the page has rendered, a card, panel or chart inside it whose shape is known shows Skeleton shapes at the loaded size, and rows inside a table already on screen use the table's own loading rows (DataTable loading with loadingRows). A region of unknown shape inside a rendered page uses Loader at base size.
rules.good: Opening a machine identity while it loads shows the page loader labeled Loading ci-deployer; the Users tab keeps its header and toolbar and shows ten loading rows in its table.
rules.avoid: A Spinner or bare Loading text as a Suspense fallback, a blank area while a page chunk loads, or a page loader over a table that is already on screen.
rules.exceptions: An inline status beside text keeps Spinner with a label, and a Button keeps its own loading state. A Suspense fallback written across several lines is not linted, so review those by hand.

rules.title: Select on state the component sets, not :has()
rules.instruction: Never write a :has() selector or a Tailwind has-*, group-has-* or peer-has-* variant. Chrome re-checks :has() on DOM changes far from the element, so one cell update in a 100-row table relayouts the whole page. Set a data attribute from what the component knows (a prop, a context report from a child, or useDescendantFlags in lib/descendant-flags.ts for slotted children) and select on that.
rules.good: TableBody sets data-has-focus from its rows' context reports, and the dim rule selects tbody[data-has-focus].
rules.avoid: tbody:has([data-focused]) > tr, or has-[>[data-slot=field]]:border on a label.

rules.title: Scope rules that set inline logical insets
rules.instruction: A rule that sets inset-inline or a logical corner radius needs a class or attribute in its subject. The build lowers those properties into :lang() selectors for older browsers, and a subject left with only :lang() is matched against every element on every style recalc.
rules.good: .viewportContent { inset-inline-start: 0 } on a classed wrapper.
rules.avoid: td[data-pin="viewport"] > * { inset-inline-start: 0 }

rules.title: A far-edge chevron needs a framed or shaded tile
rules.instruction: A trailing chevron sits at the far edge only on a tile with its own ground: Tile draws a line-soft border on a bare surface and swaps it for the tint shade inside a framed Card, List or DataTable. On an unframed item, put the chevron right after the content it leads from, as a ghost Button with iconRight does.
rules.good: Three billing summary tiles in a Card, each on the tint shade with its chevron at the tile's end, or a plain label and value followed directly by a chevron.
rules.avoid: Three unframed label and value pairs spread across a row, each with its chevron pushed to the far edge of an invisible column.
